item.text:
**7B.9 — Félix Tshisekedi (2024)**  
**Bottom line:** Mostly negative. There is some real counterevidence on technocratic appointments and oversight institutions, but the year still shows strong signs of patronage politics, opaque procurement, ally placement, and repression of critics/media.

| Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|
| *DR Congo president appoints country’s first female prime minister* | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/ | Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa, a planning minister and technocrat, after weeks of coalition uncertainty. This is the clearest positive sign against pure patronage in appointments, though it is limited and does not by itself show a clean anti-nepotism pattern. | 7B.9; 7B.5 |
| *DR Congo names new government after months of delay* | Reuters | 2024-05-29 | https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/DR-Congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/ | Reuters says cabinet formation was delayed by internal jostling for jobs, and the final cabinet remained larger than expected despite pressure to cut costs. This points toward coalition bargaining and patronage rather than insulated, merit-based appointments. | 7B.9; 7B.5 |
| *Portrait of Doudou Fwamba Likunde: the new face of finance in the DRC* | ACP | 2024-05-30 | https://acp.cd/economie/rdc-fwamba-likunde-un-technocrate-rompu-a-la-tete-du-ministere-des-finances-par-elysee-kakese/ | The finance ministry was given to a career public-finance technocrat with technical credentials and ministry experience. This is a genuine counterexample to blanket clientelism, because it shows at least one strategic portfolio staffed on competence grounds. | 7B.9; 7B.5; 7B.8 |
| *Congo election commission overspent, awarded opaque contracts- report* | Reuters | 2024-01-15 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-election-commission-overspent-awarded-opaque-contracts-report-2024-01-15/ | A civil-society report said CENI could not account for about $400 million and used opaque procurement. That is strong negative evidence for procurement integrity and against transparent, non-clientelist administration. | 7B.9; 7B.7; 7B.8 |
| *Le Chef de l’État a assisté à l’ouverture de la session extraordinaire du conseil supérieur de la Cour des comptes* | Présidence RDC | 2024-10-07 | https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/le_chef_de_l_etat_a_assiste_a_louverture_de_la_session_extraordinaire_du_conseil_superieur_de_la_cour_des_comptes | The presidency said Tshisekedi backed the Court of Accounts’ control function, and the court credited him with helping revive anti-corruption oversight and public-finance control. This is the strongest positive evidence for tolerance of formal accountability institutions. | 7B.9; 7B.7 |
| *Congo President Tshisekedi draws criticism over constitutional reform plans* | Reuters | 2024-10-24 | https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-over-constitutional-reform-plans-2024-10-24/ | Tshisekedi launched a constitutional review process that critics said could remove term limits and open the door to a third term. This is strong evidence of self-entrenchment pressure and opportunistic reversal around formal commitments. | 7B.9; 7B.8; 4B.1 |
| *Media Freedoms Should Not Be a Target in DR Congo* | Human Rights Watch | 2024-07-17 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/07/17/media-freedoms-should-not-be-target-dr-congo | HRW says journalists were targeted and media freedom remained under pressure during 2024. This is relevant to the “access to public information” part of 7B.9 because it shows the state did not consistently protect independent reporting. | 7B.9; 7B.7; 7B.6 |
| *East and Southern Africa: Journalists targeted amid ongoing crackdown on media* | Amnesty International | 2024-05-03 | https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/05/media-freedom-under-threat/ | Amnesty reported that Congolese authorities closed down a dozen media outlets and programs on charges like false rumors and incitement, and that journalist Stanis Bujakera was convicted despite weak evidence. This is direct negative evidence for free information flow and against non-retaliatory governance. | 7B.9; 7B.7; 7B.6 |

**Assessment**
- **Mostly negative overall.**
- Best positive evidence: Suminwa and Fwamba appointments, plus Court of Accounts / IGF support.
- Best negative evidence: opaque election procurement, cabinet bargaining and ally placement, third-term constitutional maneuvering, and press repression.
- **Search gap:** I did not find a strong 2024 source showing direct presidential pardons or a clear nepotistic family appointment by Tshisekedi himself. The evidence base is therefore strongest on patronage, procurement opacity, and information control, and weaker on literal nepotism/pardons.
